evals.prompt: What's in flight right now?
evals.expected_output: Dispatches to references/status.md without asking the user which mode to use. Globs memory-bank/working/plans/*/plan.md and memory-bank/working/handoffs/*/handoff.md, shows the non-terminal plans table (top 5, most recent by date-prefixed id) and the open handoffs panel, then names exactly one next varde-change mode. Reads only — no plan, task, or handoff file is written or modified.
assertions: Reports status without asking the user to choose a mode
Derives status from files on disk, not from conversation memory or inference
Leaves every plan, task, and handoff file byte-identical
Recommends exactly one next mode and stops there rather than running it

evals.prompt: I want to add rate limiting to the public API. Let's figure out what that involves.
evals.expected_output: Dispatches to references/plan-start.md — the request defines scope rather than naming a concrete change to make. Creates plan.md from the initial prompt before asking anything, seeded with a best-guess Problem/Solution and unknowns routed into ## Open Questions / ## Assumptions, reports the path, then works the open questions one per turn. Authors no task files and writes no production code.
assertions: Creates a plan rather than asking the user which mode to use
Creates plan.md seeded with a best guess before asking the first question
Produces exactly one file — plan.md — with no ## Tasks section and no tasks/ files
Changes no production source during planning
Asks questions inline as a numbered menu, not via a native question-prompt tool

evals.prompt: The retry backoff in src/queue/worker.mjs is using a fixed delay — make it exponential with jitter.
evals.expected_output: Dispatches to references/build-micro-change.md. This is a clear micro-change, so build persists a bounded JSON contract, initializes its review subject, obtains a reviewer-authored approval record, and passes the start checkpoint, then edits src/queue/worker.mjs, runs the narrowest relevant check (the repository's node --test suite), and reports the result without creating plan or task artifacts. Before implementation, obtains independent pre-edit review of scope, verification, assumptions, and structural risk. Stops if that reviewer is unavailable; human decisions go to persisted planning. Carries the verdict through execution and performs implementation review only when structural risk requires it.
assertions: Implements exponential backoff with jitter in src/queue/worker.mjs
Reports running a test command, and the repository's tests pass on the changed worker
Creates no plan or task artifacts for the micro-change
Changes production source for the requested bounded change
Captured execution events show an independent reviewer approved the actual plan before the first implementation edit; coordinator prose alone is not evidence

evals.prompt: Did we actually finish 2026-08-10-manage-command? Show me the evidence.
evals.expected_output: Dispatches to references/verify.md. Resolves the plan at memory-bank/working/plans/2026-08-10-manage-command/plan.md, states its frontmatter status, reads the ## Acceptance criteria items, runs each assert: command and judges each retrieve: criterion against the named files, then reports passed / failed / unavailable with the command output or quoted line behind each. Ticks no checkbox and changes no task status.
assertions: Leaves production source unchanged, reporting evidence instead of building fixes
Grades against each criterion's assert:/retrieve: clause rather than trusting the checkbox state
Leaves plan.md acceptance checkboxes and every task status exactly as found
Reports the missing compatibility checker as unavailable and the legacy return value as failed
Recommends varde-change build if fixes are needed rather than making them

evals.prompt: Build out the whole notifications feature.
evals.expected_output: Dispatches to references/orchestrate.md. With no group named, finds the notifications group because its frontmatter is shape: group and its nested children remain incomplete. Presents that group for selection, then stops without dispatching children or editing source until the user selects it.
assertions: Identifies the request as orchestration of the existing notifications group without creating a new plan
Discovers the notifications group and names both nested child plans (schema and delivery)
Asks the user to select the discovered group without claiming any child ran
Leaves group plans and production source unchanged before selection

evals.prompt: Go over the auth changes I just made and tell me what's wrong with them.
evals.expected_output: Does not dispatch to any varde-change mode. Reviewing a diff belongs to varde-review report, which the description's 'Not for explaining or reviewing code' boundary excludes. Names varde-review rather than treating the request as a build or verify.
assertions: Does not route to build, verify, or any other varde-change mode
Names varde-review as the owner of the request
Modifies no source files

evals.prompt: Run the named notifications group end to end.

Orders schema before delivery from depends_on, builds the schema child first, and finds its one task already `blocked` on a product decision. Halts immediately: runs no later child, merges nothing, and reports the blocked child, its task, and the reason.
assertions: Orders the schema child before delivery using the declared dependency
Builds the schema child and finds its task blocked, halting immediately
Never builds or edits the delivery child
Reports the blocked child, task, and reason without merging anything

Records cause and verification after the fix
Fixes the reported symptom: invalidating a namespace evicts its namespaced entries
Adds a regression test that fails on the seeded source and passes after the fix
Captured execution events show an independent reviewer approved the actual plan before the first implementation edit; coordinator prose alone is not evidence

evals.prompt: Diagnose the cache invalidation regression described in ISSUE.md only. Do not modify production source.

Reports reproduction and tested hypotheses
States evidence limits without claiming a fix

Records the answer in Decisions so far after the user resolves it
Does not re-ask after Decisions so far already records the answer

assertions: Ignores shift words inside fenced code blocks

evals.expected_output: Each child has independent pre-edit approval; the first child completes acceptance, conclusion, and lessons, then returns its diff/branch state to orchestrate without showing or executing a finish choice. After the group completes, it shows the aggregate diff and one applicable Merge / Push and open PR / Keep as is menu, recommending Merge for the created worktree; it waits for the user's choice before merging or pushing.
assertions: No per-child finish choice interrupts the unattended group build
The second child runs after the first succeeds
Exactly one aggregate finish menu offers applicable Merge, Push and open PR, and Keep as is choices
No merge, push, PR creation, or worktree cleanup happens before the user chooses
Describes implementation review once on the aggregate applicable scope when structural risk requires it, rather than an automatic per-task review loop

assertions: Leaves src and test byte-identical to the seed when independent review is unavailable
Reports reviewer unavailability and stops without treating self-review as independent approval
